shortDescription: Manage LDAP device authentication settings on BIG-IP

options.name: bind_dn
options.description: Specifies the distinguished name for the Active Directory or LDAP server user ID. The BIG-IP client authentication module does not support Active Directory or LDAP servers that do not perform bind referral when authenticating referred accounts. Therefore, if you plan to use Active Directory or LDAP as your authentication source and want to use referred accounts, make sure your servers perform bind referral.

options.name: bind_password
options.description: Specifies a password for the Active Directory or LDAP server user ID.

options.name: ca_cert
options.description: Specifies the name of an SSL certificate from a certificate authority (CA). To remove this value, use the reserved value C(none).

options.name: check_member_attr
options.description: Checks the member attribute of the user in the remote LDAP or AD group.

options.name: client_cert
options.description: Specifies the name of an SSL client certificate. To remove this value, use the reserved value C(none).

options.name: client_key
options.description: Specifies the name of an SSL client key. To remove this value, use the reserved value C(none).

options.name: fallback_to_local
options.description: Specifies the system uses the Local authentication method if the remote authentication method is not available. Option only available on C(TMOS 13.0.0) and above.

options.name: login_ldap_attr
options.description: Specifies the LDAP directory attribute containing the local user name that is associated with the selected directory entry. If this parameter is not specified, when configuring LDAP device authentication for the first time, the default port is C(samaccountname).

options.name: port
options.description: Specifies the port the system uses for access to the remote host server. When configuring LDAP device authentication for the first time, the default port is C(389) if this parameter is not specified.

options.name: provider
options.description: A dict object containing connection details.

options.name: referrals
options.description: Specifies whether automatic referral chasing should be enabled. Option only available on C(TMOS 15.1.0) and above.

options.name: remote_directory_tree
options.description: Specifies the file location (tree) of the user authentication database on the server.

options.name: scope
options.description: Specifies the level of the remote Active Directory or LDAP directory the system should search for the user authentication.

options.name: servers
options.description: Specifies the LDAP servers the system must use to obtain authentication information. You must specify a server when you create an LDAP configuration object.

options.name: source_type
options.description: Specifies the auth source for user authentication, should be used with C(use_for_auth).

options.name: ssl
options.description: Specifies whether the system uses an SSL port to communicate with the LDAP server.

options.name: state
options.description: When C(present), ensures the device authentication method exists. When C(absent), ensures the device authentication method does not exist. When C(state) equal to (absent), before you can delete the LDAP configuration, the system must set auth to some alternative. The system ships with a system auth called C(local), therefore the system authentication type is set to that value on the device upon removal of LDAP configuration.

options.name: update_password
options.description: C(always) always updates the C(bind_password). C(on_create) only sets the C(bind_password) for newly created authentication mechanisms.

options.name: use_for_auth
options.description: Specifies whether or not this auth source is put in use on the system. If C(true), the module sets the current system auth type to the value of C(ldap). If C(false), the module sets the authentication type to C(local), similar behavior to when C(state) is C(absent), without removing the configured LDAP resource.

options.name: user_template
options.description: Specifies the distinguished name of the user who is logging on. You specify the template as a variable that the system replaces with user-specific information during the logon attempt. For example, you could specify a user template such as C(%s@siterequest.com) or C(uxml:id=%s,ou=people,dc=siterequest,dc=com). When a user attempts to log on, the system replaces C(%s) with the name the user specified in the Basic Authentication dialog box, and passes that as the distinguished name for the bind op

options.name: validate_certs
options.description: Specifies whether the system checks an SSL peer, as a result of which the system requires and verifies the server certificate.
